name: Honey-soy glazed salmon
steps: Put the rinsed rice in a saucepan with 2¼ cups water, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low for 15 minutes; take it off the heat and let it steam, covered, for 10 minutes.
Heat the oven to 425°F and line a sheet pan with foil.
Toss the broccoli with the oil and salt on one side of the pan and roast for 8 minutes.
Meanwhile stir together the soy sauce, honey, rice vinegar, garlic and ginger to make the glaze.
Push the broccoli aside, lay the salmon skin side down on the pan and brush it generously with the glaze.
Roast 10 to 12 minutes, until the salmon reaches 145°F in the thickest part or flakes easily with a fork, brushing on the last of the glaze halfway.
Serve the salmon and broccoli over the rice, sprinkled with scallions and sesame seeds.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, brush slices of tofu with a spoonful of the glaze and roast them on the pan beside the salmon.

ingredients.note: patted dry, sliced ½ inch thick

name: Lemon-herb crumb cod
side: Roasted green beans and crusty bread.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Toss the green beans with the olive oil and ¼ tsp salt on a sheet pan and roast for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile mix the panko, melted butter, lemon zest, parsley, garlic and ¼ tsp salt in a bowl.
Push the green beans to the edges, set the cod in the middle and season it with the remaining salt and the pepper.
Press the crumb mixture onto the tops of the fillets.
Bake 10 to 12 minutes, until the crumbs are golden and the fish reaches 145°F or flakes easily with a fork.
Squeeze lemon wedges over the fish and serve with the green beans and crusty bread.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, toss a drained can of white beans with a few spoonfuls of the crumb mixture in a small baking dish and bake it alongside for 12 minutes.

name: Tilapia fish tacos with lime slaw
side: Lime slaw, avocado and lime crema.
mildNote: Use 1 tsp chili powder, or season the kids' pieces with just cumin, garlic powder and salt.
steps: Toss the cabbage with half the lime juice, the cilantro and a pinch of salt and set aside.
Stir the sour cream with the remaining lime juice and a pinch of salt to make the crema.
Mix the chili powder, cumin, garlic powder and the rest of the salt, and rub it over both sides of the fish.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the fish 3 to 4 minutes per side, until it reaches 145°F and flakes easily with a fork; work in batches if needed.
Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet for about 30 seconds per side, keeping them wrapped in a towel.
Break the fish into chunks and fill the tortillas with fish, slaw, avocado and a drizzle of crema.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, warm a can of black beans in a small pan with a pinch of the spice mix and use it in place of the fish.

name: Tuna cakes with lemon mayo
side: Romaine salad with lemon and olive oil.
steps: In a bowl mix the tuna, eggs, panko, 3 tbsp of the mayo, the Dijon, scallions, lemon zest and pepper until it holds together.
Shape into 8 patties about ¾ inch thick and chill them for 10 minutes so they hold their shape.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat and cook the cakes 3 to 4 minutes per side, until deep golden and firm in the center.
Stir the remaining mayo with 1 tbsp of the lemon juice to make the lemon mayo.
Toss the romaine with the olive oil, the rest of the lemon juice and the salt.
Serve the tuna cakes with the lemon mayo and the salad.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, mash a drained can of chickpeas with a little of the egg, panko and Dijon, shape into 2 to 3 cakes and fry them the same way.

name: New England cod chowder
steps: Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onion and celery for 5 minutes, until soft.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute, then slowly whisk in the broth so no lumps form.
Add the potatoes, thyme, bay leaf and salt, bring to a boil, then simmer 12 to 15 minutes, until the potatoes are tender.
Stir in the milk and corn and heat until steaming and barely simmering; don't let it boil hard.
Add the cod and simmer gently 5 to 6 minutes, until it is opaque, reaches 145°F and flakes easily.
Remove the bay leaf, season with the pepper and serve with crusty bread.
Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, ladle 1 to 2 portions into a small pot before adding the cod and simmer a drained can of white beans in it for 5 minutes.

name: Shrimp and broccoli stir-fry
steps: Simmer the rice with 2¼ cups water, covered, on low for 15 minutes, then let it rest off the heat for 10 minutes.
Whisk the soy sauce, hoisin, cornstarch, sesame oil and ½ cup water in a small bowl.
Heat 1 tbsp vegetable oil in a large skillet over high heat, stir-fry the broccoli for 2 minutes, add 3 tbsp water, cover and steam 2 minutes, then move it to a plate.
Add the remaining oil and the shrimp and stir-fry 2 to 3 minutes, until pink and opaque all the way through.
Add the garlic and ginger and stir for 30 seconds.
Return the broccoli, pour in the sauce and stir for about 1 minute, until glossy and thickened. Serve over the rice.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, brown cubes of tofu in a small skillet and toss them with a few spoonfuls of the sauce and some of the broccoli.

name: Spaghetti with tuna, tomato and capers
side: A green salad, if you like.
mildNote: Leave out the chili flakes and pass them at the table for the adults.
steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil with 1 tbsp salt.
Warm the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat and cook the garlic and chili flakes for 1 minute, until fragrant but not browned.
Add the crushed tomatoes, capers, olives and 1 tsp salt and simmer 10 minutes, stirring now and then.
Meanwhile cook the spaghetti according to the package, about 10 minutes, and save ½ cup of the pasta water before draining.
Stir the tuna into the sauce and warm it through for 2 minutes.
Toss the spaghetti with the sauce, adding splashes of pasta water to loosen it, and sprinkle with parsley.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, set aside a portion of the sauce before the tuna goes in and warm a drained can of white beans in it.

name: Seared scallops with lemon orzo and peas
side: Lemony orzo with peas and Parmesan.

ingredients.note: thawed overnight in the fridge, patted very dry

steps: Melt 1 tbsp butter in a saucepan over medium heat, add the orzo and toast it for 2 minutes, stirring.
Pour in the broth, bring to a simmer and cook 10 to 12 minutes, stirring often, until the orzo is tender and creamy; stir in the peas for the last 2 minutes.
Take the orzo off the heat and stir in the Parmesan and lemon zest; cover to keep warm.
Season the scallops with the salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Sear the scallops without moving them for 2 minutes, until a golden crust forms, then flip.
Add the remaining 2 tbsp butter and the garlic and spoon the butter over the scallops for 1 to 2 minutes, until they are opaque all the way through.
Squeeze the lemon juice over the scallops and serve them on the orzo with the pan butter.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, stir a drained can of white beans into a portion of the orzo while it finishes cooking.

name: Chipotle shrimp burrito bowls
side: Cilantro-lime rice, black beans, corn and avocado.
mildNote: Use half a chipotle, or set aside the kids' shrimp tossed with just cumin, garlic, oil and salt before adding the chipotle.
steps: Simmer the rice with 2¼ cups water and ½ tsp salt, covered, on low for 15 minutes, rest 10 minutes, then stir in the lime juice and half the cilantro.
Toss the shrimp with the chipotle, garlic, cumin, 1 tbsp oil and the remaining salt.
Warm the black beans and corn together in a small saucepan over medium heat for 5 minutes.
Heat the remaining oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the shrimp 2 to 3 minutes, flipping once, until pink and opaque all the way through.
Build bowls with rice, beans and corn, shrimp and avocado, then top with sour cream, the rest of the cilantro and lime wedges.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, warm a second can of black beans with a pinch of cumin and use it in place of the shrimp.

name: Miso salmon with soba and bok choy
side: Sesame soba noodles with bok choy.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F and line a sheet pan with foil.
Stir the miso, honey and 1 tbsp rice vinegar into a paste and spread it over the tops of the salmon on the pan.
Roast 12 to 14 minutes, until the salmon reaches 145°F or flakes easily; if the glaze darkens too fast, lay a piece of foil loosely on top.
Meanwhile bring a large pot of water to a boil and cook the soba according to the package, usually 4 to 5 minutes, adding the bok choy for the last 2 minutes.
Drain and rinse briefly under warm water, then toss with the soy sauce, sesame oil, ginger and the remaining rice vinegar.
Serve the salmon on the noodles and bok choy, topped with scallions and sesame seeds.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, spread a little of the miso glaze on slices of tofu and roast them beside the salmon.

ingredients.note: patted dry, sliced ½ inch thick

name: Cajun tilapia with corn, zucchini and peppers
mildNote: Leave out the cayenne; the smoked paprika is smoky, not hot.
steps: Simmer the rice with 2¼ cups water and ¼ tsp salt, covered, on low for 15 minutes, then let it rest off the heat.
Heat the oven to 425°F. Mix the smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, thyme, cayenne and 1 tsp salt.
Toss the zucchini, peppers and corn on a sheet pan with 2 tbsp oil and half the spice mix, and roast 15 minutes.
Brush the fish with the remaining oil and rub it with the rest of the spice mix.
Push the vegetables to the sides, lay the fish in the middle and roast 8 to 10 minutes, until it reaches 145°F and flakes easily with a fork.
Serve with the rice and lemon wedges.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, toss a drained can of chickpeas with a pinch of the spice mix and roast them with the vegetables.

name: Thai green curry shrimp
mildNote: Start with 1 tbsp curry paste (brands vary a lot in heat) and serve the kids' portions with extra rice.
steps: Simmer the rice with 2¼ cups water, covered, on low for 15 minutes, then let it rest off the heat for 10 minutes.
Heat the oil in a large deep skillet over medium heat and fry the curry paste for 1 minute, stirring, until fragrant.
Stir in the coconut milk, fish sauce and brown sugar and bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the bell pepper and snap peas and simmer 3 minutes.
Add the shrimp and simmer 3 to 4 minutes, until pink and opaque all the way through.
Stir in the basil and lime juice and serve over the rice with lime wedges.

name: Smoky shrimp and cheesy grits
mildNote: Leave out the cayenne; the smoked paprika adds flavor without heat.
steps: Bring the milk, 2 cups water and ¾ tsp salt to a simmer in a saucepan, then slowly whisk in the cornmeal.
Cook on low for 15 to 20 minutes, whisking often, until thick and creamy; stir in the butter and cheddar and cover to keep warm.
Toss the shrimp with the smoked paprika, cayenne and the remaining salt.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the shrimp for 2 minutes without moving them, then flip.
Add the garlic and tomatoes and cook 1 to 2 minutes more, until the shrimp are pink and opaque all the way through and the tomatoes soften.
Squeeze in the lemon juice and spoon the shrimp and tomatoes over the grits, topped with scallions.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, top a bowl of grits with a fried egg and some of the tomatoes cooked before the shrimp.

name: Salmon burgers with dill yogurt sauce
steps: Chop the salmon with a sharp knife into small bits, then mix it with the panko, egg, Dijon, scallions, lemon zest, 2 tbsp dill, ½ tsp salt and the pepper.
Shape into 4 patties about ¾ inch thick and chill for 15 minutes so they hold together.
Stir the yogurt with the remaining dill, 1 tbsp lemon juice and the rest of the salt.
Heat the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat and cook the burgers about 4 minutes per side, until browned and 145°F in the center.
Serve on the toasted buns with lettuce and the dill yogurt sauce.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, mash a drained can of chickpeas with a little of the egg, panko, Dijon and dill, shape into patties and cook them the same way.

name: Tuna melts
steps: Mix the tuna, mayo, celery, red onion, Dijon, lemon juice and pepper in a bowl.
Spread the tuna on 4 slices of bread and top with tomato slices, cheddar and the remaining bread.
Butter the outsides of the sandwiches.
Cook in a large skillet over medium-low heat 3 to 4 minutes per side, until golden and the cheese has melted; cover the pan for the last minute to help it melt.
Cut in half and serve with the cucumber and carrot sticks.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, make a grilled cheese with extra cheddar and tomato slices.

name: Lemon shrimp and asparagus risotto
side: A squeeze of lemon and extra Parmesan.
steps: Warm the broth in a saucepan over low heat.
In a large pot, melt 1 tbsp butter with the oil over medium heat and cook the shallots 3 minutes, then add the garlic and rice and stir for 1 to 2 minutes.
Add the warm broth a ladle at a time, stirring often and letting it absorb before adding more, for about 18 to 20 minutes, until the rice is creamy and just tender.
Stir in the asparagus after about 12 minutes of adding broth.
Add the shrimp for the last 4 to 5 minutes and cook until pink and opaque all the way through.
Off the heat, stir in the remaining butter, the Parmesan, lemon zest and juice, salt and pepper, and serve right away.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, spoon 1 to 2 portions into a small pan before adding the shrimp and warm a drained can of white beans in it.

name: Cod in tomato, olive and caper sauce
steps: Heat the oil in a large skillet with a lid over medium heat and cook the onion 5 minutes, until soft.
Add the garlic and oregano and cook 1 minute.
Stir in the tomatoes, olives, capers and ¼ tsp salt and simmer 10 minutes, until slightly thickened.
Season the cod with the remaining salt and the pepper and nestle it into the sauce.
Cover and simmer gently 8 to 10 minutes, until the fish reaches 145°F and flakes easily with a fork.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve with crusty bread.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, spoon some sauce into a small pan before adding the fish and simmer a drained can of chickpeas in it.

name: Coconut fish curry
mildNote: Use a mild curry powder; it's warmly spiced rather than hot, and the coconut milk softens it further.
steps: Simmer the rice with 2¼ cups water and a pinch of salt, covered, on low for 15 minutes, then rest 5 minutes off the heat.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat and cook the onion 6 to 8 minutes, until golden.
Add the garlic and ginger for 1 minute, then the curry powder and turmeric for 30 seconds.
Stir in the tomatoes and simmer 5 minutes, then add the coconut milk and the rest of the salt and simmer 5 minutes more.
Add the cod and simmer gently, without stirring too much, 6 to 8 minutes, until it reaches 145°F and flakes easily.
Stir in the lime juice, sprinkle with cilantro and serve over the rice with lime wedges.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, ladle some sauce into a small pan before adding the fish and simmer a drained can of chickpeas in it for 5 minutes.

name: Tuna noodle casserole
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F and boil the noodles 2 minutes less than the package says, then drain.
Melt 2 tbsp butter in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onion and mushrooms 6 minutes, until soft.
Stir in the flour for 1 minute, then slowly whisk in the milk and simmer 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until thickened.
Off the heat, stir in the salt, pepper and cheddar, then fold in the noodles, tuna and peas.
Spread in a 9x13-inch baking dish. Melt the remaining butter, toss it with the panko and scatter it over the top.
Bake 20 minutes, until bubbling and golden. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, spoon 1 to 2 portions into a small baking dish before the tuna goes in, stir in a drained can of white beans and bake it alongside.

name: Shrimp pad thai
mildNote: Leave the sriracha out of the sauce and pass it at the table.
steps: Soak the noodles in very hot tap water for 8 to 10 minutes, until bendable but still firm, then drain.
Whisk the fish sauce, brown sugar, rice vinegar, lime juice and sriracha until the sugar dissolves.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large skillet over high heat and cook the shrimp 2 to 3 minutes, until pink and opaque, then move them to a plate.
Add the remaining oil, the garlic and carrot and stir for 1 minute, then push them aside, pour in the eggs and scramble until set.
Add the noodles and sauce and toss with tongs for 2 to 3 minutes, until the noodles are tender and have soaked up the sauce.
Toss in the shrimp and scallions and serve topped with peanuts and lime wedges.

name: Tuna Niçoise salad
side: Warm potatoes, green beans and eggs.
steps: Put the potatoes in a pot of cold water with ½ tsp salt, bring to a boil and cook 12 to 15 minutes, adding the green beans for the last 3 to 4 minutes, until both are tender; drain.
Meanwhile lower the eggs into a small pot of boiling water, cook 10 minutes, then cool in cold water, peel and halve.
Whisk the shallot, Dijon, vinegar, olive oil, pepper and the rest of the salt in a large bowl.
Toss the warm potatoes and green beans with half the dressing.
Arrange the romaine on a platter and top with the potatoes, green beans, tuna, tomatoes, olives and eggs.
Drizzle with the remaining dressing and serve.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, use a drained can of chickpeas in place of the tuna on their plates.

name: Sheet-pan shrimp fajitas
side: Warm tortillas, sour cream and lime.
mildNote: Halve the chili powder, or toss the kids' shrimp with just cumin, garlic powder and salt.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F and mix the chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika, garlic powder and salt.
Toss the peppers and onion on a sheet pan with 2 tbsp oil and half the spice mix and roast 15 minutes.
Toss the shrimp with the remaining oil and spice mix.

Stir the vegetables, scatter the shrimp over them and roast 6 to 8 minutes, until the shrimp are pink and opaque all the way through; wrap the tortillas in foil and warm them in the oven at the same time.
Squeeze the lime juice over the pan and serve in the tortillas with sour cream, cilantro and lime wedges.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, warm a drained can of black beans with a pinch of the spice mix in a small pan and tuck them into the fajitas.

name: Pesto salmon with roasted tomatoes
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Set the salmon on a sheet pan, season with half the salt and the pepper, and spread the pesto over the tops.
Toss the tomatoes with the olive oil and scatter them around the fish.
Roast 12 to 15 minutes, until the salmon reaches 145°F or flakes easily and the tomatoes blister.
Meanwhile bring the broth and the rest of the salt to a boil in a saucepan, stir in the spinach until it wilts, then stir in the couscous.
Cover, take off the heat and let it stand 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork and stir in the lemon zest and juice.
Serve the salmon and tomatoes on the couscous.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, toss a drained can of chickpeas with a spoonful of pesto and roast them beside the tomatoes.

name: Tilapia piccata
side: Spaghetti tossed in the lemon-caper sauce.

ingredients.note: plus more for the pasta water

steps: Cook the spaghetti in well-salted boiling water according to the package, then drain.
Season the fish with the salt and pepper and dredge it lightly in the flour, shaking off the extra.
Heat the oil and 1 tbsp butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the fish in two batches, 2 to 3 minutes per side, until golden, 145°F and flaking easily; move to a plate.
Lower the heat to medium, add the garlic for 30 seconds, then pour in the broth, lemon juice and capers and simmer 2 to 3 minutes, scraping up the browned bits.
Turn off the heat and swirl in the remaining 2 tbsp butter until the sauce is glossy.
Toss the spaghetti with half the sauce, top with the fish, spoon over the rest and sprinkle with parsley.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, toss a portion of the spaghetti and sauce with a drained can of white beans.

name: Gochujang shrimp rice bowls
mildNote: Before adding the gochujang, set aside the kids' shrimp tossed with just soy sauce, honey and sesame oil, or halve the gochujang.
steps: Simmer the rice with 2¼ cups water, covered, on low for 15 minutes, then let it rest off the heat for 10 minutes.
Toss the cucumber and carrots with the rice vinegar, 1 tsp honey and the salt and set aside to pickle.
Whisk the gochujang, soy sauce, sesame oil, garlic and the remaining 1 tbsp honey.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the shrimp 2 minutes, then flip.
Pour in the sauce and toss for 1 to 2 minutes, until the shrimp are glazed, pink and opaque all the way through.
Serve the shrimp over rice with the pickled vegetables, scallions and sesame seeds.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, brown tofu cubes in a small skillet and toss them with a spoonful of the gochujang sauce.

name: Potato, pepper and cheddar frittata
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a 10- to 12-inch oven-safe skillet over medium heat, add the potatoes, cover and cook 10 to 12 minutes, stirring now and then, until tender.
Add the onion and bell pepper and cook uncovered 5 minutes more, until soft.
Whisk the eggs with the milk, paprika, ¾ tsp salt, the pepper and half the cheddar, pour over the vegetables and cook without stirring for 3 to 4 minutes, until the edges set.
Scatter the remaining cheddar on top and bake 12 to 15 minutes, until the center is set with no runny egg when you cut into it (160°F).
Let it rest 5 minutes while you toss the arugula with the last 1 tbsp oil, the lemon juice and the remaining salt. Cut the frittata into wedges and serve with the salad.

name: Mushroom, spinach and cheddar strata

ingredients.note: plus a little for the dish

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F and butter a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the mushrooms and onion 8 to 10 minutes, until browned and the liquid has cooked off; stir in the spinach.
Spread half the bread in the dish, top with half the vegetables and half the cheddar, then repeat the layers.
Whisk the eggs, milk, Dijon, ¾ tsp salt and the pepper, pour evenly over the bread and press down so it soaks in; let it stand 15 minutes (or cover and refrigerate overnight).
Bake 45 to 50 minutes, until puffed and golden and a knife in the center comes out clean (160°F); rest 5 minutes.
Toss the romaine with the olive oil, vinegar and the remaining salt and serve alongside. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

name: Sweet potato and pinto bean enchiladas
side: Sour cream and cilantro on top.
mildNote: Red enchilada sauce is usually mild; leave out the chili powder for sensitive kids.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the sweet potato and onion with the oil, cumin, chili powder and salt on a sheet pan and roast 20 to 25 minutes, until tender.
Lower the oven to 375°F. In a bowl, roughly mash half the beans, then stir in the rest of the beans, the roasted vegetables and 1 cup cheese.
Spread ½ cup enchilada sauce in a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Divide the filling among the tortillas, roll them up and set them seam side down in the dish.
Pour the remaining sauce over the top, sprinkle with the rest of the cheese and bake 20 minutes, until bubbling.
Top with sour cream and cilantro and serve.

name: Mediterranean quinoa and chickpea salad
side: Feta, olives and a lemon-oregano dressing.
steps: Bring the quinoa and 3 cups water to a boil, cover and simmer on low for 15 minutes, until the water is absorbed.
Let it stand covered off the heat 5 minutes, then spread it on a plate to cool for 10 minutes.
Whisk the lemon juice, olive oil, garlic, oregano, salt and pepper in a large bowl.
Add the quinoa, chickpeas, cucumber, tomatoes, red onion, olives and parsley and toss well.
Top with the feta and serve warm or cold. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

name: Crispy tofu and broccoli in garlic-ginger sauce
steps: Wrap the tofu blocks in a clean towel and press under a heavy pan for 10 minutes, then cube them. Meanwhile simmer the rice with 2¼ cups water, covered, on low for 15 minutes and let it rest.
Toss the tofu with 2 tbsp cornstarch. Heat 2 tbsp oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat and fry the tofu 8 to 10 minutes, turning, until golden and crisp; move to a plate.
Whisk the soy sauce, honey, rice vinegar, sesame oil, the remaining 1 tbsp cornstarch and ½ cup water.
Add the remaining oil and the broccoli to the pan, stir 1 minute, add 3 tbsp water, cover and steam 3 minutes.
Add the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds, pour in the sauce and stir about 1 minute, until thickened.
Return the tofu, toss to coat and serve over the rice with sesame seeds.

name: Black bean burgers
side: Lettuce, tomato and melted cheddar on buns.
steps: Mash the beans with a fork or potato masher, leaving some pieces whole.
Stir in the oats, egg, diced onion, garlic, cumin, smoked paprika and salt, then shape into 4 patties and chill 10 minutes.
Heat the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat and cook the patties 4 to 5 minutes per side, until crisp and hot all the way through (160°F, since they contain egg).
Lay the cheddar on the burgers for the last minute and cover the pan to melt it.
Serve on the buns with lettuce, tomato and sliced red onion.

name: White bean minestrone
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onion, carrots and celery 8 minutes, until soft.
Add the garlic and Italian seasoning and cook 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, broth, beans, salt and pepper, bring to a boil, then simmer 10 minutes.
Stir in the zucchini and pasta and simmer 8 to 10 minutes, until the pasta is tender.
Ladle into bowls and top with Parmesan. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours; the pasta will soak up broth, so add a splash of water when reheating.

name: Southwestern stuffed peppers
side: Sour cream and cilantro on top.
mildNote: Use mild salsa and leave out the chili powder.
steps: Simmer the rice with 1½ cups water, covered, on low for 15 minutes, then let it rest off the heat.
Heat the oven to 400°F. Brush the pepper halves with the oil, sprinkle with half the salt and set them cut side up in a 9x13-inch dish with ¼ cup water; cover with foil and bake 15 minutes to soften.
Mix the rice with the beans, corn, salsa, cumin, chili powder, the remaining salt and 1 cup cheese.
Fill the peppers, top with the rest of the cheese and bake uncovered 15 to 20 minutes, until the filling is hot and the cheese is browned.
Serve two halves each with sour cream and cilantro.

name: Lentil sloppy joes
steps: Simmer the lentils in the broth in a covered saucepan for 20 to 25 minutes, until tender and most of the liquid is absorbed; drain any extra.
Meanwhile heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat and cook the onion and pepper 6 to 8 minutes, until soft.
Add the garlic and tomato paste and stir 1 minute.
Stir in the tomato sauce, brown sugar, soy sauce, smoked paprika and salt and simmer 5 minutes.
Add the lentils and simmer 5 minutes more, until thick enough to pile on a bun.
Spoon onto the buns, two per person, and serve with carrot sticks.

name: Matar paneer
mildNote: Leave out the cayenne; garam masala is warm rather than hot.
steps: Simmer the rice with 2¼ cups water and a pinch of salt, covered, on low for 15 minutes, then rest 5 minutes off the heat.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and brown the paneer 4 to 5 minutes, turning, then move it to a plate.
Add the remaining oil and the onion and cook over medium heat 8 minutes, until golden; add the garlic and ginger for 1 minute.
Stir in the garam masala, cumin, turmeric and cayenne for 30 seconds, then add the tomato sauce, ½ cup water and the salt and simmer 8 minutes.
Add the peas and paneer and simmer 5 minutes, until the peas are hot.
Stir in the cream and serve over the rice.

name: Huevos rancheros
side: Refried black beans, avocado and lime.
mildNote: Use mild salsa; everything else is mild.
steps: Warm the beans, garlic, cumin, salt and ¼ cup water in a saucepan over medium heat for 5 minutes, mashing them roughly with a potato masher; keep warm. Warm the salsa in a small pan.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and crisp the tortillas one or two at a time, 30 to 60 seconds per side; drain on paper towels.
Lower the heat to medium, add the remaining oil and fry the eggs 3 to 4 minutes, until the whites are fully set; cover the pan for firm yolks for young kids.
Spread beans on two tortillas per plate, top each with an egg, warm salsa and cheese.
Finish with avocado, cilantro and lime wedges.

name: Spinach and ricotta lasagna roll-ups

ingredients.note: plus more for the pasta water

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F. Boil the noodles in salted water 2 minutes less than the package says, drain and lay them flat on a sheet of foil brushed with the oil.
Mix the ricotta, spinach, 1 cup mozzarella, the Parmesan, egg, garlic, Italian seasoning, nutmeg, salt and pepper.
Spread 1 cup marinara in a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Spread about ¼ cup filling along each noodle, roll it up and set it seam side down in the dish.
Spoon the rest of the marinara over the rolls and sprinkle with the remaining mozzarella.
Cover with foil and bake 25 minutes, then uncover and bake 10 to 15 minutes more, until bubbling and hot in the center (165°F); rest 5 minutes before serving.

name: Peanut noodles with tofu and edamame
side: Crunchy cucumber and carrots on top.
mildNote: Leave the sriracha out of the sauce and pass it at the table.
steps: Heat the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat and fry the tofu 8 to 10 minutes, turning, until golden; splash in 1 tbsp soy sauce and toss.
Cook the spaghetti in boiling water according to the package, adding the edamame for the last 3 minutes; save ½ cup of the cooking water, then drain.
Whisk the peanut butter, the remaining 3 tbsp soy sauce, rice vinegar, honey, sriracha, ginger and garlic with ¼ cup of the hot cooking water until smooth.
Toss the noodles, edamame and carrots with the sauce, adding more cooking water if it's too thick.
Serve topped with the tofu, cucumber and scallions, warm or cold. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

name: Sweet and sour tofu with pineapple

ingredients.note: peeled, cored and cut into chunks (about 2 cups)

steps: Simmer the rice with 2¼ cups water, covered, on low for 15 minutes, then let it rest off the heat.
Toss the tofu with 3 tbsp cornstarch. Heat 2 tbsp oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat and fry the tofu 8 to 10 minutes, turning, until crisp; move to a plate.
Whisk the rice vinegar, brown sugar, tomato paste, soy sauce, the remaining 1 tbsp cornstarch and ½ cup water.
Add the remaining oil, the peppers and onion to the pan and stir-fry 3 to 4 minutes, until crisp-tender; add the pineapple and garlic for 1 minute.
Pour in the sauce and stir about 1 minute, until thick and glossy.
Fold in the tofu and serve over the rice.

name: Tomato soup with cheddar grilled cheese
steps: Melt 2 tbsp butter in a pot over medium heat and cook the onion 6 to 8 minutes, until very soft, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the crushed tomatoes, broth, sugar, basil, salt and pepper, bring to a boil and simmer 15 minutes; mash with a potato masher if you like it smoother.
Stir in the half-and-half and heat until steaming, without boiling.
Meanwhile make 4 sandwiches with the bread and cheddar and spread the outsides with the remaining butter.
Cook the sandwiches in a large skillet over medium-low heat 3 to 4 minutes per side, until golden and the cheese melts.
Cut the sandwiches into strips and serve with the soup.

name: Cuban-style black bean soup
side: Sour cream, cilantro and tortilla chips.
mildNote: Leave out the jalapeño, or cook it in a little oil separately and stir it into the adults' bowls.
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onion, bell pepper and jalapeño 8 minutes, until soft.
Add the garlic, cumin and oregano and stir for 1 minute.
Add the beans, broth and salt, bring to a boil, then simmer 15 minutes.
Mash about half the beans right in the pot with a potato masher to thicken the soup.
Stir in the lime juice and serve topped with sour cream, cilantro and tortilla chips. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

name: Moroccan chickpea and sweet potato stew
mildNote: It's warmly spiced but has no chili heat, so it's kid-friendly as is.
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onion and carrots 6 minutes, until softened.
Add the garlic, cumin, ginger and cinnamon and stir for 1 minute.
Add the sweet potato, tomatoes, broth, chickpeas, raisins and ¾ tsp salt, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer 20 minutes, until the sweet potato is tender.
Meanwhile bring 1¾ cups water and the remaining salt to a boil, stir in the couscous, cover, take off the heat and let it stand 5 minutes; fluff with a fork.
Serve the stew over the couscous. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

name: Lentil shepherd's pie

ingredients.note: divided, plus more for the potato water

steps: Heat the oil in a large deep skillet over medium heat and cook the onion and carrots 8 minutes, then add the garlic, tomato paste and thyme and stir 1 minute.

Add the lentils, broth and 1 tsp salt, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer 25 to 30 minutes, until the lentils are tender; uncover for the last 5 minutes so it thickens. Stir in the peas and pepper.
Meanwhile cover the potatoes with cold salted water, bring to a boil and cook 15 to 20 minutes, until very tender; drain.
Mash the potatoes with the butter, warm milk and the remaining salt.
Heat the oven to 400°F. Spread the lentil filling in a 9x13-inch baking dish, top with the mashed potatoes and rough up the surface with a fork.
Bake 20 minutes, until bubbling at the edges and golden on top. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

name: Baked eggplant Parmesan

ingredients.note: plus more for the pasta water

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F and brush two sheet pans with 2 tbsp of the oil.
Mix the panko, ½ cup Parmesan, Italian seasoning and salt. Dip each eggplant slice in egg, then press it into the crumbs and set it on the pans.
Drizzle with the remaining oil and bake 20 to 25 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden and tender. Lower the oven to 375°F.
Spread 1 cup marinara in a 9x13-inch dish, layer half the eggplant, 1 cup marinara and half the mozzarella, then repeat and finish with the rest of the Parmesan.
Bake 20 minutes, until bubbling, then scatter the basil on top.
Meanwhile cook the spaghetti in salted boiling water according to the package, drain and toss with the remaining marinara, warmed. Serve with the eggplant.

name: Warm French lentil salad with goat cheese
steps: Simmer the lentils with the garlic, thyme and 4 cups water for 20 to 25 minutes, until tender but holding their shape; drain and remove the garlic.
Meanwhile heat the oven to 425°F, toss the carrots with 1 tbsp oil and ¼ tsp salt on a sheet pan and roast 20 minutes, until tender.
Lower the eggs into boiling water, cook 9 minutes, cool in cold water, then peel and halve.
Whisk the shallots, Dijon, vinegar, the remaining 4 tbsp oil, the rest of the salt and the pepper in a large bowl.
Toss the warm lentils, carrots and parsley in the dressing.
Serve over the arugula, topped with goat cheese and the eggs.

name: Baked gnocchi with white beans and mozzarella
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Warm the oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium heat, add the garlic for 1 minute, then stir in the tomatoes, Italian seasoning, salt and ½ cup water and bring to a simmer.
Stir in the gnocchi, beans and spinach, a handful at a time, until the spinach wilts, and simmer 3 minutes.
Top with the mozzarella and Parmesan and bake 15 to 20 minutes, until the gnocchi are tender and the cheese is bubbling and browned.
Scatter the basil over the top and serve. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

name: Cheese tortellini primavera

ingredients.note: plus more for the pasta water

steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
Heat the oil and butter in a large skillet over medium heat and cook the zucchini 4 minutes, until lightly browned; add the garlic and tomatoes and cook 2 minutes, until the tomatoes soften.
Cook the tortellini according to the package, usually 3 to 4 minutes, adding the peas for the last minute; save ½ cup of the cooking water and drain.
Add the tortellini and peas to the skillet with the lemon zest and juice, Parmesan, salt, pepper and a splash of cooking water, and toss until glossy.
Top with basil and serve.

name: Miso udon soup with tofu and eggs
steps: Lower the eggs into boiling water and cook 7 minutes, then cool in cold water, peel and halve.
Bring the broth, ginger, garlic and soy sauce to a simmer in a large pot and cook 5 minutes.
Add the mushrooms and simmer 3 minutes, then the bok choy for 2 to 3 minutes, then the tofu for 2 minutes to heat through.
Meanwhile cook the udon in a separate pot of boiling water according to the package, usually 2 to 3 minutes, and drain.
Turn the soup off, whisk the miso with a ladle of the hot broth until smooth and stir it back into the pot; don't let it boil after this.
Divide the noodles among bowls, ladle over the soup and top with the eggs, scallions and a few drops of sesame oil.

name: Baked falafel pitas
side: Cucumber, tomato and tahini yogurt sauce.

ingredients.note: drained, rinsed and patted very dry
half finely chopped, half thinly sliced

steps: Heat the oven to 400°F and brush a sheet pan with 2 tbsp oil.
Mash the chickpeas well with a potato masher, then mix in the chopped onion, 2 cloves garlic, the parsley, cumin, flour and ¾ tsp salt until it holds together.
Shape into 12 small patties, set them on the pan and brush the tops with the remaining oil.
Bake 25 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden and crisp on both sides.
Stir the yogurt, tahini, lemon juice, the last clove of garlic and the remaining salt into a sauce.
Warm the pitas in the oven for the last 2 minutes and fill them with falafel, cucumber, tomato, sliced onion and sauce.

name: Spinach and feta puff pastry pie

ingredients.note: thawed in the fridge overnight or 40 minutes on the counter

steps: Heat the oven to 400°F and line a sheet pan with parchment.
Mix the spinach, feta, ricotta, 3 eggs, scallions, dill, nutmeg and pepper in a bowl.
Lay one pastry sheet on the pan, spread the filling over it leaving a 1-inch border, then lay the second sheet on top and press the edges together with a fork.
Beat the last egg and brush it over the top, then cut a few small slits for steam.
Bake 35 to 40 minutes, until deep golden and puffed and the filling is hot and set in the middle (160°F); rest 10 minutes before cutting into squares.
Toss the cucumber and tomatoes with the olive oil, vinegar and salt and serve alongside. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
